waypoints.name: Mount Teneriffe Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-90 Exit 32 (436th Ave SE), turn north over the freeway and drive 0.5 mile to SE North Bend Way. Turn left, and in 0.25 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road. In 2.9 miles, past the Little Si and Mount Si trailheads, the paved Mount Teneriffe Trailhead lot is on the left. A Discover Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Teneriffe Falls Trail junction
waypoints.directions: Climb the access trail as it switchbacks through second-growth forest, then turn left onto the old logging-road grade and follow it gently to the signed junction for Teneriffe Falls.

waypoints.name: Teneriffe Falls / Kamikaze Trail junction
waypoints.directions: Turn right onto the Teneriffe Falls Trail and follow it about 1.9 miles, gently at first and then up many switchbacks, to the viewpoint below the falls. The Kamikaze track leaves a few yards back from the upper viewpoint.

waypoints.name: Mount Teneriffe Summit
waypoints.directions: Climb the steep, unofficial Kamikaze track, which goes round the falls on climber's right and climbs the fall line on roots and rock to the southwest ridge, then follow the ridge crest through meadow and a rock band to a short scramble at the summit.

waypoints.name: Goodell Creek / Upper Goodell Group Camp trailhead (SR-20, Newhalem)
waypoints.directions: Turn north off Highway 20 directly across from Newhalem Campground onto the unpaved Goodell Creek Road and follow it to the Upper Goodell Creek Group Camp trailhead at about 600 ft. A North Cascades National Park wilderness permit is required for any overnight stay; this cross-country zone is walk-up only, issued in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

waypoints.name: Mount Terror summit
waypoints.directions: Follow the old roadbed along Goodell Creek about 4.5 miles, cross Terror Creek, and climb the steep, pink-flagged climbers' track past moss-covered cliffs into Crescent Creek Basin, nearly 6,000 ft of gain to camp. From the basin climb the narrow, loose west gully to the chockstone notch between Terror and The Rake, then about 100 ft of low fifth-class crack and 250 ft of class 3 to the summit.
